root_idea.summary: The root centers on return: something comes back to a former place, condition, or intended state.
root_idea.development: From return and recurrence develop meanings of gathering, restoration, recompense as what returns to a person, a place of repeated return, and a garment repeatedly worn.

senses.definition: To recompense or requite someone for what they have done.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is passive: the unbelievers are described as being recompensed for their deeds. The recompense need not be favorable.

senses.definition: To recompense, requite, or reward someone for an act.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage the recompense may be favorable, as a reward for good, or adverse, as requital for hardship or suffering. The construction takes the person receiving the recompense as its object.

senses.definition: A place to which people return repeatedly and gather.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic description of the Sacred House, the word also admits the interpretation of a place associated with attaining the reward of pilgrimage; the central image remains repeated return and assembly.

senses.definition: Recompense, requital, or reward returned to a person for an act.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses the word both for a favorable reward and, by an adverse extension, for a bad recompense or requital.

senses.definition: Recompense or reward returned for an act, especially a good act.
senses.usage_conditions: The term can apply to good or evil recompense, but Quranic usage most often presents it as a favorable reward, including reward from God in this world or the next.

senses.definition: A garment or item of clothing worn on the body.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural ثِيَاب refers to garments or clothing, including clothing worn, changed, or provided in ordinary contexts.

senses.definition: To purify one's garments, and by extension one's personal or moral state, in the expression وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction is interpreted literally as purifying or shortening garments and figuratively as purifying oneself, the heart, conduct, or moral condition. These are interpretations of the same garment-purification construction, not a restriction to any particular type of clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To return to a place or to a former condition; to come back after departing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same return construction extends to repentance, renewed attentiveness, restored health, and the return of reason or forbearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water, to return or collect again after being drawn or diminished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of well water or water in a trough that regains its former level or collects again.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of people, to gather and come, often company after company.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This collective use is applied to a group rather than a solitary person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become abundant through gathering or accumulation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied classically to property that becomes plentiful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of dust, to rise, spread, or become abundant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension describing dispersed matter that gathers or increases.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a watering-trough or tank, to become full or nearly full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The image is of water returning until the receptacle is replenished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To restore someone or something to a former or better condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical applications include restoring richness after poverty, bodily soundness after leanness, or an upright condition after decline.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To call or summon repeatedly, especially by making a second call.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is used for repeated summonses and for the repeated call associated with the adhan.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To repeat or add a prayer call, and in later usage to perform prayer after the prescribed prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The prayer-call usage includes the iqāmah and other repeated announcements; the supererogatory-prayer usage is identified as post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become one termed ثَيِّب, a person who has previously entered the marriage state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited derived-verb usage is feminine and describes becoming ثَيِّب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To return repeatedly to someone as a suitor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited construction describes suitors coming back to the woman time after time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause water to return after it has stopped or diminished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a valley or well whose water supply returns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To restore a person or thing to bodily soundness, richness, or an upright condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited applications include restoring the body after leanness and setting an inclined or disordered matter upright again.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give something in exchange for, or as compensation for, another thing or a gift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the substitution or compensation construction, distinct from simply rewarding a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sew a garment or piece of cloth a second time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb describes the second, more complete sewing after an initial light or running stitch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill or nearly fill a watering-trough or tank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative counterpart to the use of ثَابَ for a receptacle becoming full.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gain or earn a recompense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage is reported as post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To restore or repossess property that had gone away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe recovering wealth through something given or obtained in exchange.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone to recompense, compensate, requite, or reward him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the causative-seeking sense of requesting recompense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing that veils, covers, or protects.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a metonymic use of a garment and can include a protective means or covering such as curtains in an idiomatic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weapons, viewed figuratively as protective equipment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical plural use derived from the protective function of garments.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The wearer's body, self, or what garments enfold; by extension, one's state or works.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This metonymy appears in expressions about a person's body, the state in which one dies, or the works accompanying one's life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In idioms, excellence or a good deed, responsibility, or separation from another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional figurative expressions based on the garment as something associated with a person or resting upon him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moral character, conduct, or reputation, described as pure or soiled clothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Expressions such as pure or dirty garments characterize freedom from fault, vice, perfidy, or an evil reputation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fetal or birth membrane surrounding what is delivered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical expression for the membrane called السَّلَى or الغِرْس.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where water collects in a valley or low ground, or the part of a trough to which water returns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is explained through the return of water to that place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company, distinct body, or troop of people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression فَانْفِرُوا ثُبَاتٍ, it denotes going forth in separate groups or troops.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Honey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative designation based on bees returning to it and on its being the good produced by bees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rain, viewed as the good resulting from the winds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical extension of recompense or returning benefit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic plural use based on their returning to the hive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who has previously entered the marriage state; especially a woman who is no longer a virgin or has separated from a husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also applied to a man, though predominantly to a woman. Classical explanations include a previously married person, one whose spouse has died or divorced her, and one who has had sexual intercourse; a broader extension may apply it to a woman who has reached puberty even if still a virgin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who takes care of clothes in a bathhouse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is identified as a post-classical occupational term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who repents or returns from disobedience to obedience frequently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A synonymic intensive designation derived from repeated return.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller or possessor of garments or pieces of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This occupational or descriptive noun is distinct from the intensive term for one who repents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water that returns after being drawn away or after the ebb.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to the returning supply of a well and to seawater flowing after ebbing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fresh, sappy herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use comparing fresh growth to the returning water of the sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A people or group arriving company after company.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression describes successive arrivals rather than one solitary person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A violent wind that blows at the beginning of rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized weather term derived from the return or arrival of rain-bearing conditions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place from which water returns to supply a well after some has been drawn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the returning-water location associated with a well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The station or brink of a well where the water-drawer stands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote the middle or brink of the well and the structures on which the water-drawer stands.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The successive stone casing or interior construction of a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning concerns the stones or walling arranged from the top to the bottom of the well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where a hunter or fowler sets a snare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place understood as one to which the hunted creature returns or is brought.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where well water collects after returning from being drawn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized well-related use distinct from the Quranic place of human return.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The projecting stones or interior walling around a well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote the stones on which a person stands or the place where the well is walled within.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The foundations of a house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural specialized use associated with the structural base of a dwelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Winds attended by prosperity or blessing and expected to produce good results, especially rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression for winds from which benefit is hoped.
